spec_match.rationale: Uses the exact spec surface — a:navigation-source styling the element that triggered the current navigation for its whole course — over real Navigation API interceptions, with the parse probe hitting the real selector via querySelector try/catch.

interactive.rationale: Real links start real (intercepted, deliberately slow) same-document navigations; the view content, mechanism chip, aria-live status and navigation log all change per click.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises the clicked link showing its own in-flight state plus the labelled JS pattern beside it; that is what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles no-selector and no-Navigation-API tiers distinctly and restores state on direct-URL load, but does not cover a second navigation interrupting the first (which navigation's source matches) — noted as an open question.

references.rationale: chromestatus.com/feature/6327898878377984, the spec section, and MDN's Navigation API page are all linked.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite pins both parser entry points, compound usage, the idle no-match invariant, the never-matching div, and records the mid-navigation matching contract as manual with the sampler named as its measuring instrument.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 via CDP: autorun clicked Reports, the log recorded start → mid-flight fallback-class true → settled/class removed, view updated, zero console errors, mobile 360 emulation overflow-free. The native selector path cannot execute on 141 (querySelector throws) and is labelled unsupported; on a 156 build the autorun's matches() sample would verify it directly.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts the probe, the explicit fallback branch, navigation completion per trip, and the autorun mid-flight state (native matches() or fallback class).

design_system.rationale: Variables only; native state (green solid) and fallback state (amber dashed) are deliberately distinct so the fallback can never impersonate native success; spinners honour prefers-reduced-motion.

accessibility.rationale: The rail is a labelled nav of real links with focus-visible outlines and 44px targets; view changes and arrival are announced via aria-live; the log is a role=log region.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: CDP-emulated 360x740 DPR3: zero horizontal overflow, no console errors, links wrap into tappable rows.

guidanceConsulted.query: show loading state on the link or submit button that started a navigation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Loading feedback should be tied to the control that initiated the action and end when the action settles.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: That is the demo's subject: the in-flight ring lives exactly as long as the navigation state, natively via :navigation-source or via the labelled fallback class removed on settle.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: State changes must have non-visual equivalents.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: aria-live status line narrates departure and arrival; the navigation log keeps a keyboard-reachable textual history.

openQuestions.title: Behaviour when a second navigation interrupts the first
openQuestions.detail: Click Inbox and then Reports before the first interception settles: per the Navigation API the first navigation aborts. Verify on a 156 build whether the first link stops matching immediately and the second starts, and journal it — the demo's log is ready to show it, but the expected result should be documented from observation, not assumption.

openQuestions.title: Cross-document lifetime needs a real two-page check
openQuestions.detail: The active-navigation-state explainer says cross-document matching runs from initiation to the new page's first frame. This demo only exercises same-document interceptions; a two-page variant under this feature folder could demonstrate the cross-document window once a 156 build is available for verification.

summary: Canonical loading-links demo: intercepted 1.2s navigations where the clicked link wears its in-flight state, natively via a:navigation-source on 156 or via a visually-distinct labelled JS fallback elsewhere. Autorun evidence on Chromium 141 shows the full lifecycle logged with clean console; native-path verification is deferred to a 156 build and recorded honestly.
